**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), fallback-level cure.**

- **What we found:** § 20(d) is a flat mutual prohibition on assignment without the other party's written consent — no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard. § 3(c) reinforces it against us only ("not assign this Agreement... except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing"). That is walk-away territory and fails all four fallback elements.
- **Change-of-control:** no such clause exists anywhere in the document (searched § 17 and globally), so Garman has no termination or re-pricing trigger on our change of control — nothing to strike there.
- **Cure (shortest, fallback):** rewrote § 20(d) to allow either party to assign to a successor to its business on written notice, with consent for any other assignment not to be unreasonably withheld; and deleted only the words "assign this Agreement or" from § 3(c) so the retained restriction on transfer, lease, export and sublicence of the Work stays intact but no longer contradicts the new assignment right.
